messages.author: fd1c548a0ef4b2ee
messages.subject: multipleGroup and DIF
parts:
Hi Phil Chalmers,

We used mirt package to estimate the latent trait (level of biosecurity in swine farms) with a scale of 14 items.
We have 604 samples divided in 4 unbalenced groups (1- ;2- ;3- ;4-) and I am using survey.weights argument to adjust for the survey complex design of the study. 

We used multipleGroup function to obtain the model (see syntax) and then for DIF analyses we used 2 methods, like you describe at help function.
First adding slopes and intercepts constraints results, then using Wald tests with Benjamini & Hochberg adjustment.

The former analyses (add a1 and d contraints) showed no DIF (No DIF items were detected for plotting) and the second showed DIF for all items.

Is the the first method of detect DIF less rigorous compared to the second?
Or did I estimate the model wrong?
Do you have some thoughts to help me?

Syntax:
+ Model:
model2 <- multipleGroup(dataset19, 1, groups, SE = TRUE, 
                        survey.weights = banco.total$pesomirt, 
                        technical = list(NCYCLES = 1000), 
                        TOL = 0.001)

+ DIF analyses 1:
resulta1d <- DIF(model2, c('a1', 'd'), plotdif = TRUE,
                 technical = list(NCYCLES = 1000), TOL = 0.001)

+ DIF analyses 2:
resulta1dWald <- DIF(model2, c('a1', 'd'), Wald = TRUE, p.adjust = 'fdr')


Thanks,
Gustavo Silva

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: multipleGroup and DIF
parts:
Hi Gustavo,

Were the latent mean/variance of the focal group freed? It doesn't look like the setup is quite right, which would indicate the different results. DIF only can be studied when the groups are properly equated; otherwise, these procedures are testing both group differences + DIF effects jointly. HTH.

Phil

parts:
Hi Phil,

Thank you so much.

I think yes, we used the argument (invariance = c(colnames(banco19.imputation), 'free_means', 'free_var'), is this correct? 

To give you more information, in the first analyses we used the syntax below.

mod.19<- mirt(banco19, 1, itemtype = '2PL', survey.weights = banco.total$pesomirt, SE=TRUE))
coef(mod.19, simplify=TRUE, IRTpars=TRUE)
scores <- fscores(mod.19)

Now, we want to check for DIF in the groups of the sample, so we used the model that I described in the first post using multipleGroup function.

If we are doing something wrong, what would be the correct specification?

Best regards,

Gustavo

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: multipleGroup and DIF
parts:
The mulipleGroup syntax is fine, but of course constraining all the item parameters to be equal across groups means that only the 'add' option would work (the drop would be meaningless as all the items are already in their simplest, group constrained form). I'm not sure I follow the rest of your question regarding the single group specification, sorry. 

Phil

Hi Phil,

I have a similar confusion here when using the 2 methods to get DIF items:

+ DIF analyses 1:
resulta1d <- DIF(model2, c('a1', 'd'), plotdif = TRUE,
                 technical = list(NCYCLES = 1000), TOL = 0.001)

+ DIF analyses 2:
resulta1dWald <- DIF(model2, c('a1', 'd'), Wald = TRUE, p.adjust = 'fdr')

For analysis 1, to be conservative, I used p=0.01. 
In this case, 3 items came up with p < 0.01.

For analysis 2, should I use 0.05, or, 0.01 (as a comparable estimate to analysis 1)? 
Here, the 3 items' p-values are between 0.01 and 0.05.
